watch_intent: Tell me when any email arrives from a sender at a domain ending in @loopstack.io that mentions a production incident, outage, or service degradation — specifically any message that includes words like 'down', 'outage', 'incident', 'degraded', 'unavailable', 'P0', or 'P1' in the subject or body.

Tell me when an email arrives from recruiting@loopstack.io, talent@loopstack.io, or any sender whose email address contains 'recruit' or 'talent' at the loopstack.io domain, and the email is about a candidate moving to offer stage, an offer being accepted or declined, or a candidate dropping out of the hiring pipeline.

Tell me when an email arrives where the sender is not from the loopstack.io domain and the subject or body explicitly mentions a contract, MSA, SOW, renewal, or pricing negotiation — I want to catch vendor or partner emails that require a decision or signature, not internal forwards or newsletters.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body mentions a sprint review, sprint planning, sprint retrospective, or quarterly planning meeting and includes a date, a calendar invite link, or a request to confirm attendance — I want to know about scheduling asks for these specific ceremonies, not just general project status updates.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the body or subject explicitly mentions a security vulnerability, CVE, data exposure, unauthorized access, or compliance audit related to Loopstack's platform or infrastructure — I want to catch inbound security disclosures or audit requests from external parties, not internal security digests or automated scanner reports.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body explicitly mentions a performance improvement plan, PIP, termination, involuntary separation, or an employee being let go — and the email either comes from an address containing 'hr', 'people', or 'peopleops' at the loopstack.io domain, or the body explicitly states it is from HR or People Operations at Loopstack. I want to catch HR-initiated actions that affect my team, not general management discussion or offboarding checklists sent to the whole company.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly mentions a paid invoice, a failed payment, a past-due balance, an upcoming auto-renewal, or a subscription charge of more than $500 — and the email is addressed to priya.nair@loopstack.io or references Loopstack by name. I want to catch billing events that require my attention or approval, not marketing emails, free-trial offers, or general pricing announcements.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body explicitly asks me, Priya Nair, to approve, review, or sign off on a technical design document, architecture decision record, or RFC — and the email includes a link or attachment and either sets a deadline or asks for a response by a specific date. I want to catch approval requests that are time-boxed, not general FYI shares of design docs or meeting notes.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender at the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body mentions an engineer resigning, giving notice, or leaving the company — or uses phrases like 'last day', 'two weeks notice', 'stepping down', or 'moving on' — and the email body explicitly states, using those words or close equivalents, either that the departing person is a member of the Platform Engineering team or platform team, or that their direct manager is Priya Nair. Acceptable phrasings that satisfy the team or manager requirement include 'Platform Engineering team', 'platform team', 'reports to Priya Nair', 'Priya's direct report', or 'Priya Nair's team'. Do not fire if the team or reporting relationship is only implied, inferable from context, or absent from the email text entirely.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly requests a technical integration, an API partnership, a co-sell arrangement, or a technology partnership with Loopstack — and the sender identifies themselves as working at a named company and includes a specific ask or next step. I want to catch inbound partnership inquiries that require a real response, not cold sales pitches for tools or services Loopstack would be buying.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender at the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly describes a CI/CD pipeline failure, a broken build, or a failed deployment to a staging or production environment — and the message names a specific service, repository, or environment such as 'production', 'staging', 'main branch', or a named service — and at least one of the following is true: (1) the email addresses me by name (Priya Nair) or by my email address and explicitly asks me to take a specific action or provide a response, not merely a generic system link; or (2) the email explicitly states that the failure has been unresolved or ongoing for more than one hour. Do not fire on routine automated pass/fail notifications that do not name a specific environment or service, or that include only generic links without a named addressee or stated unresolved duration.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly mentions a reference check, a background check request, or a request to verify employment for a named individual who is described as a current or former employee at Loopstack — and the sender identifies themselves as working at a named company or staffing agency and includes a specific question or form to complete. I want to catch inbound reference or verification requests that require my direct response, not automated background-check platform notifications or internal HR process emails.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body explicitly mentions a headcount freeze, a hiring pause, a budget cut affecting engineering headcount, or a reduction in open engineering requisitions — and the email either comes from an address containing 'finance', 'cfo', 'hr', 'people', or 'exec' at the loopstack.io domain, or the body explicitly states it is from Finance, the CFO, HR, or an executive at Loopstack. I want to know about decisions that would affect my team's planned hiring, not general company budget updates or all-hands recaps.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly describes a bug, regression, or unexpected behavior in Loopstack's product — and the sender identifies themselves as a paying customer or enterprise account, and the email either requests escalation, mentions a specific ticket or account number, or states that the issue is blocking their team's work. I want to catch inbound customer-reported technical escalations that have been sent directly to me or forwarded to me with an explicit ask, not automated support ticket notifications or internal bug triage summaries.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender at the loopstack.io domain, or from a sender at pagerduty.com, opsgenie.com, or victorops.com, where the primary purpose of the email is to communicate a change to an on-call rotation schedule or an alerting policy — meaning the email's main subject is the schedule update or policy change itself, not a page about or summary of an active or resolved incident — and the email explicitly names the Platform Engineering team or explicitly identifies the affected rotation as belonging to Platform Engineering — and the email either requests my approval or acknowledgment, or describes a change that takes effect on a stated future date. Do not fire if the email's primary purpose is to notify about an active incident, a resolved incident, or a status page update, even if that email incidentally references on-call assignments or rotation names.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender at the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly mentions a post-mortem, incident review, or root cause analysis document that is ready for review or has been shared for feedback — and the email names a specific incident, date, or affected service — and the email explicitly requests my review, input, or approval by addressing me by name (Priya Nair), by my email address, or by my role, rather than sending a generic team-wide or company-wide review request. Do not fire on automated incident alert summaries, incident notification emails, or general engineering retrospectives that do not include an explicit, individually directed request for my review or sign-off.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly mentions a conference talk submission, a CFP (call for proposals or call for papers), or an invitation to speak or present at a named technical conference or developer event — and the email is addressed to me by name (Priya Nair) or to my email address priya.nair@loopstack.io, and includes a specific deadline or response window. I want to catch speaking invitations and CFP opportunities that require a real decision, not mass newsletter announcements about upcoming conferences or event sponsorship pitches.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body explicitly mentions a third-party dependency, open-source library, or infrastructure component that Loopstack uses — and the email describes a breaking change, a deprecated API, an end-of-life announcement, or a mandatory upgrade with a stated deadline. The sender can be internal or external, but the email must name a specific package, service, or version and either state a cutoff date or describe an action required from an engineering team. I want to catch forced migration or upgrade notices that could affect the platform team's roadmap, not general release notes or changelog digests.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender where the subject or body explicitly asks me, Priya Nair, to provide a performance review, written feedback, or a promotion recommendation for a named individual — and the email either comes from an address containing 'hr', 'people', or 'peopleops' at the loopstack.io domain, or the body explicitly states it is from HR or People Operations at Loopstack — and the email includes a deadline or a link to a review form or system. I want to catch structured performance or promotion review requests that have a due date, not informal peer feedback requests or general reminders about the review cycle sent to all managers.

Tell me when an email arrives from any sender outside the loopstack.io domain where the subject or body explicitly describes a legal hold, litigation hold, or e-discovery request that names Loopstack or references Loopstack employees, systems, or data — and the sender identifies themselves as an attorney, law firm, or legal representative and includes a specific request for document preservation or production. I want to catch inbound legal hold or discovery notices that require immediate action, not general legal newsletter updates, terms-of-service change notifications, or internal legal process reminders.
